slides.title: Double the radius. The volume does ==not== double.

slides.stem: Sphere A has a radius of r and sphere B has a radius of 2r. The volume of sphere B is how many times the volume of sphere A?
slides.prompt: Time yourself. Comment your time and your answer.

slides.title: D — 8
slides.body: Linear ratio is 2; volume scales by its cube: 2³ = 8. Most students pick A (2): used the linear ratio directly, forgetting volume cubes it.

slides.title: Pure Volume Scaling
slides.body: Doubling the radius multiplies volume by 8; tripling by 27; halving divides by 8. Volume is always the cube of the linear ratio.
